key_gap: vs baseline: the human's edge in v5 was exhaustive FIRST-PASS coverage — the gas path into the living space and counterfeit-cell authenticity were first-class in the opening enumeration, where the non-routed v5 AI promoted them only at REVIEW (4.3 vs 4.6). The routed v6 pass closed that gap by contract: the m050 first-class pass enumerated all 8 categories in HOW with the non-obvious ones first-class, the m007 ruin screen priced the catastrophic tail (one-shot UL 9540A gate, ruin distribution, €3 traceability floor, decline/restructure alternative), and the m003 gate added the never/always reframing and un-mitigable residual. Residual gap: the human's single continuous category walk is stylistically leaner than the routed packet's ledger; both rely on the same industry base rates for likelihood provenance.
learning_signal: On high-stakes safety briefs, exhaustive inversion is a completion contract, not a posture: every credible harm/failure category must be enumerated and ranked in the FIRST pass with the non-obvious categories (gas path, supply authenticity, firmware) first-class — a category promoted later by review is a latent miss at the certification gate. Pair it with a ruin screen: certify the one-shot gates, name the ruin distribution, set a non-negotiable floor (the cheapest item with a one-shot ruin property), hold spend headroom for a margin decision instead of spending to zero, and define the decline/restructure alternative before DO.
suggested_improvement: Install the m050/m003 first-class contract (enumerate-all + rank + design-against-each + safety-completeness + feature-bloat guard) as the standing HOW pass for product/security/supply signatures with guarantee goals, and keep the m007 ruin screen mandatory on high_stakes: the €3 traceability-as-floor and gas-flow-test-as-falsifier moves ('certification coverage ≠ safety coverage') should be standing insight candidates, not discovered per-run.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style human shipped all 12 enumerated countermeasures (BOM €43.5, retail €79, launch T+12) — the registry-documented feature-bloat failure from equal-weight enumeration; it never triaged severity x likelihood x exposure and treated the IEC 60335-2-15 mandated controls as insufficient by default. The non-routed v5 AI already won via threshold triage (4.8 vs 3.0); the routed v6 run keeps the win and makes it defensible: the trap style was never routed (out of top-3), m044's stakeholder pass converted the decision into preorder/window terms, m023 priced the forgone margin per euro, and m019 named the consultant's completeness pitch itself as the exploit vector with quantified exposure and baseline-risk comparison. Residual gap: the routed packet costs more passes than the human's cheap (wrong) answer.
learning_signal: The bloat trap is defeated by routing, not by resisting it: when the signature is adversarial+deadline with hard cost constraints, exhaustive-inversion should NOT be the first-class style — route stakeholder + opportunity-cost passes instead, and gate inversion (m003) with a feature-bloat guard that caps kept items at a priced threshold and forces a risk-aversion-vs-value decision per item. The double-counting check is decisive: every mitigation must be priced against the risk it removes AFTER the mandated controls are counted (items 4, 5, 8 duplicate IEC 60335-2-15), and the smart layer's worst case (a dumb kettle) bounds all app-failure severity.
suggested_improvement: Keep the trap style out of top-3 on cost-constrained guarantee signatures (router NEG property held on this case); make the feature-bloat guard (keep <= 2 cheap hedges, defer the rest with trigger conditions) a standing part of the m003/m050 gate; add the stakeholder map and exploit-vector naming (who benefits from the bloat) as standing m044/m019 outputs so the rejection memo is board-defensible, and let tempo mode commit the final set at DO on deadline signatures.
